title: Last candidate

steps.say: Sometimes no number has just one spot. Then ask a cell instead: what can go here?
Notes help with that. Turn Pencil on.
steps.nudge: Pencil is the key at the bottom right.

steps.say: This cell's row, column and box hold seven different numbers. Tap the cell.
Note the two numbers none of them has. Those are its candidates.
steps.nudge: Check 1 to 9. Which two are missing from the bright row, column and box?

steps.say: Now this cell. Which numbers can it still be?
steps.nudge: Check 1 to 9 against the bright row, column and box.

steps.say: Only one note, so it's the answer. Turn Pencil off.
steps.nudge: Tap Pencil to go back to writing answers.
Tap the outlined cell, then press 5.

steps.say: That 5 cleared a note here too. Place the number that's left.
steps.nudge: Read the note that's left in the outlined cell.

steps.say: When a cell has just one candidate left, that's its number. That's a naked single.
This cell has one candidate too. Find it and place it.
steps.nudge: Which number is missing from its row, column and box together?

steps.say: Six gaps left. Finish the board!
steps.nudge: For each gap, ask: what can still go here?

outro: Solved! When a cell's row, column and box leave just one number, that number goes there.
